subject: Inference transition playbook & migration options (ShopWise)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Barnes <sophie@shopwise.ai>, Chris Taylor <ctaylor@shopwise.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: inference transition playbook & next steps

Hi Sophie / Chris — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before I build the POA.

Recap of what I heard (please correct me if I missed anything):
- Primary product: real-time recommendations for top-of-funnel site personalization (ShopWise web + mobile).
- Current traffic pattern: steady baseline with predictable peaks during promotions (spikes ~3x baseline for 2–3 hours).
- Current infra: on-prem Nvidia cluster (DGX hosts) for legacy models + third-party LLM API for spikes.
- Security/compliance: must keep PII out of long-term logs; procurement requires SOC2 evidence and VPC connectivity.
- Timeline: decision target by end of Q2; pilot ideally in the next 4–6 weeks.

Questions we need to close to recommend a migration mode:
1) Is full data residency required on-prem for inference, or is a VPC/Private deployment acceptable?
2) Expected qps (steady-state / peak) for the inference routes we’d move first — can you share the sheet you mentioned?
3) Any hard constraints on tokenization (max prompt length) or latency SLOs (p95 target)?
4) Do you have a procurement window or preferred contract cadence (monthly vs annual)?

Recommended next steps (short list):
- Share the traffic estimates (attachment stub: shopwise-mvp-traffic-estimates.xlsx).
- Quick security check: I’ll attach our SOC2 one-pager and the standard VPC network checklist (attached: redwood-quick-tiers.pdf).
- I propose we evaluate three paths in parallel (short descriptions below) and agree which path to pilot first:
  A) Hosted API pilot (fastest): spin up a scoped PoC against your spike route to validate latency and integrations; minimal procurement.
  B) Dedicated reserved pool (predictable): reserved GPUs for steady traffic + burst for promotions; good if you need consistent throughput and isolated capacity.
  C) Private (VPC / on-prem connector): customer-managed networking with optional on-prem inference connector for full residency. Best for regulated or fully air-gapped needs.

If you’re comfortable, I’ll draft a mutual action plan (timeline + success criteria) for each path and we can pick one to start. Marissa (CS) and Tessa (Solutions) are looped in to scope the pilot and the security questions.

Attachments: redwood-quick-tiers.pdf (pricing tiers & quick SOC2 note); shopwise-mvp-traffic-estimates.xlsx (requested)

Thanks — Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Sophie Barnes <sophie@shopwise.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Chris Taylor <ctaylor@shopwise.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference transition playbook & next steps

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers inline below and I attached the architecture diagram you asked for.

Inline answers:
1) Residency: We need customer data to remain in our AWS account/region. We cannot forward production PII outside our VPC, so a Private deployment or VPC-peered Hosted/Dedicated option is preferred.
2) Traffic: For the MVP route (recommendations), steady qps ~45 req/s; peaks ~140 req/s during campaigns. I attached the small traffic sheet as well.
3) Latency: p95 target <120ms for the page render path; we can tolerate slightly higher for batch background jobs.
4) Procurement: Procurement prefers annual contracts but will sign a 3-month pilot MSA to validate performance.

Notes and constraints:
- We currently rely on a mix of in-house DGX servers (for older models) and a third-party LLM API that we use for unpredictable spikes. Moving off the third-party API for the spike traffic is a priority because of cost unpredictability.
- Security: we’ll need your SOC2 report, the VPC peering checklist, and an IP allowlist for the pilot.

Attached: current-architecture-diagram.png; traffic estimates (embedded in Drive link)

Sophie
Sophie Barnes
Head of ML Engineering, ShopWise Inc.
sophie@shopwise.ai | +1 (212) 555-0112

On Sun, May 30, 2027 at 2:12 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Sophie / Chris — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference transition playbook & next steps

Thanks Sophie — that’s very helpful. Based on what you shared, here are concise migration-mode recommendations and a proposed pilot scope for us to discuss on the follow-up call: 

Short mode comparison (pros / cons):
- Hosted API pilot
  Pros: fastest to validate model/latency, low procurement friction.
  Cons: requires either token redaction or strict prefix caching to avoid PII egress; may not meet your VPC residency requirement without peering.
- Dedicated reserved capacity
  Pros: predictable throughput, billing, and opaque capacity pooling; can be VPC-peered for isolated networking.
  Cons: longer procurement lead time for reserved commitments; good fit if steady qps is sustained.
- Private (VPC / on-prem connector)
  Pros: full control, supports on-prem connector to keep inference within customer network, best for compliance.
  Cons: longest setup and ops coordination; may require on-call runbooks and network approvals.

Pilot recommendation (short):
1) Start with a scoped Hosted API PoC for the MVP route to validate latency and integration (2 weeks). Use token redaction + prefix cache in the PoC and run synthetic loads to reproduce p95.
2) Parallel security readiness: Redwood to supply SOC2 summary + VPC peering checklist; you to confirm IP allowlist and procurement pilot MSA.
3) If PoC meets latency and cost targets, progress to Dedicated reserved pool for baseline traffic and burst for campaigns (30–60 day transition). If residency is non-negotiable, proceed directly to Private VPC option and scope on-prem connector workstreams.

Action items I’ll own:
- Draft three short mutual action plans (Hosted PoC / Dedicated / Private) with timeline & success criteria — I’ll share by EOD Wednesday.
- Prep SOC2 summary and VPC checklist (attached: redwood-quick-tiers.pdf).

Can we lock a 30-minute follow-up slot on Thursday to agree which pilot to run first? I’ll include Marissa to estimate costs and Tessa to scope the engineering work.

Thanks — Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Looping in a quick commercial view — I agree with Karthik’s staged approach. Practical notes from procurement perspective: 
- Pilot MSA: we can offer a 90-day pilot MSA with a limited spend cap and an easy stop clause. That should satisfy your procurement team.
- Pricing rough split for evaluation: Hosted PoC (metered) -> Dedicated (monthly commit) -> Private (one-time integration + lower per-token). I’ll prepare a short estimate doc once Karthik shares the mutual action plans.

Security ops note for the thread: I will request a SOC2 redacted copy and the VPC peering checklist from our security team; Karthik, please share the inbound IP ranges we’ll need to add to ShopWise allowlist.

Next steps I recommend we confirm on the Thursday slot:
- Which path to pilot first (expected: Hosted PoC with VPC peering question).
- Confirm timeline for pilot sign-off (target: sign MSA by June 10).
- Marissa to share initial cost estimate in separate email after Karthik’s action plans.

Thanks — Marissa
